terms.title: Bond yield
terms.summary: The yearly return a bond pays, as a percentage of its price. When a bond's price falls, its yield rises, and the other way round. Government yields show what it costs a government to borrow.

terms.title: Yield curve
terms.summary: A line joining the yields of government bonds from short terms (one month) to long terms (30 years). It usually slopes up. When short-term yields are higher than long-term ones, the curve is called inverted.

terms.title: Basis point
terms.summary: One hundredth of a percentage point (0.01%). A yield moving from 4.20% to 4.25% has risen 5 basis points. Rate changes are often quoted this way, or in percentage points (pt).

terms.title: Bond
terms.summary: A loan to a government or company that pays interest and returns the amount lent on a set date. Its price and its yield move in opposite directions: when the price falls, the yield to a new holder rises.
